guide.title: Periods and effective multipliers
guide.periodBody: Match by time and weekday. Other periods applies outside the listed windows; All periods applies when no windows are configured.
guide.currentBody: Current marks the matching period only. It does not mean the route or provider is enabled.
guide.factorBody: These are combined multipliers including the provider multiplier, not monetary amounts.
guide.chargedFormula: Effective billing = active provider multiplier × billing multiplier
guide.meteredFormula: Effective cost = active provider multiplier × cost multiplier
guide.validityBody: Every row is previewed as of now. Before the provider multiplier starts or after it expires, ×1 applies. A clock icon indicates that it is currently inactive.
guide.scopeTitle: The price used as the baseline
guide.scopeBody: Each multiplier is relative to that period’s catalog price, which already includes the catalog schedule multiplier. Do not apply it again. User-specific multipliers and final billed amounts are not included.
guide.hint: Hover over a multiplier for its calculation and validity dates.

effectivePricing.inactiveProvider: The provider multiplier is inactive; ×1 is used in this calculation.

editor.mappingDescription: Connect the model requested by clients to its upstream provider.
editor.headersDescription: HTTP headers sent with requests to the upstream.
editor.headersEmpty: No custom headers. Use the add button above to create one.
editor.bodyDescription: Add upstream request parameters as a JSON object.
editor.pricingTimezone: Multipliers apply to catalog rates · Timezone {timezone}
editor.providerFactorHelp:
A provider discount or markup applied to both user billing and provider cost.
For example, 0.8 applies 80% on both sides; 1 makes no adjustment. Outside its validity period, ×1 applies.
editor.chargedFactorHelp:
Adjusts the amount charged to the user without changing provider cost.
Effective billing multiplier = provider multiplier × billing multiplier.
For example, 0.8 × 0.5 = 0.4: charge 40% of the catalog price for that period.
This route preview excludes user-specific multipliers.
editor.meteredFactorHelp:
Adjusts provider cost without changing the amount charged to the user.
Effective cost multiplier = provider multiplier × cost multiplier.
For example, 0.8 × 0.3 = 0.24; enter 0 to record zero cost.
editor.effectiveFactorHint: Effective multiplier = currently active provider multiplier × this multiplier; excludes the catalog time multiplier.
editor.catalogPricesHint: Prices include the catalog multiplier for each period.
editor.billingFactorsHint: Charges and supply costs are calculated separately. The supplier multiplier applies to both.
editor.rowValidityHint: Applies only to this row’s supplier multiplier. Uses ×1 outside its validity. Leave blank for no limit. Timezone: {timezone}.
editor.pricesAtCurrentDate: Prices use this period’s supplier validity at the current date; before it starts or after it expires, the supplier multiplier is ×1.
editor.defaultFactorsHint: Billing and supply cost are calculated separately. The provider multiplier applies to both.

adapterDescriptions.passthrough: Forwards the request and response unchanged. Client and upstream protocol and operation must match.
adapterDescriptions.dashscope-asr-qwen-file: OpenAI transcription (multipart) → Qwen3-ASR sync API. For qwen3-asr-flash and similar; do not use for Qwen-Audio-3.0.
adapterDescriptions.dashscope-asr-qwen-audio-file: OpenAI transcription (multipart) → Qwen-Audio-3.0 sync API; language maps to language_hints. For qwen-audio-3.0-asr-flash.
adapterDescriptions.dashscope-asr-file-async: OpenAI transcription + public file_url → filetrans async submit and poll. The provider needs both the submit and task query endpoints.
adapterDescriptions.dashscope-tts-speech: OpenAI /v1/audio/speech → SpeechSynthesizer. For CosyVoice and Qwen-Audio-3.0-TTS; supports mp3, opus, wav, pcm and speed 0.5–2.0.
adapterDescriptions.dashscope-tts-qwen: OpenAI /v1/audio/speech → Qwen-TTS multimodal API. For qwen3-tts-flash and similar; returns wav only and does not support speed. OpenAI instructions is written to input.instructions and applies only to the Instruct-Flash series. For Qwen-Audio-3.0-TTS, choose CosyVoice / Qwen-Audio-3.0 TTS.
adapterDescriptions.dashscope-tts-minimax: OpenAI /v1/audio/speech → MiniMax multimodal API. Supports mp3, pcm, flac, and wav. OpenAI instructions is not mapped; set emotion in the route request parameters at input.voice_setting.emotion.
adapterDescriptions.dashscope-image-qwen: OpenAI Images → Qwen Image multimodal-generation. size must be in pixels (such as 1024x1024).
adapterDescriptions.minimax-asr-file: OpenAI transcription (multipart) → MiniMax speech_to_text. Set the provider model name to asr-1.0. language is sent as a request header; the gateway renders srt and vtt from timestamped segments.
adapterDescriptions.minimax-tts: OpenAI /v1/audio/speech → MiniMax t2a_v2. Provider model names are speech-2.8-hd or speech-2.8-turbo. voice is a MiniMax voice_id. Supports mp3, pcm, flac, and wav. speed is 0.5–2. stream_format=sse becomes OpenAI speech events.
adapterDescriptions.minimax-image: OpenAI /v1/images/generations → MiniMax image_generation. Provider model names are image-01 or image-01-live. size such as 1024x1024 is mapped to the nearest aspect_ratio. response_format url or b64_json is returned as OpenAI data[].

strategy.title: Route strategy
strategy.protocolLevelHint: Leave empty to resolve through model endpoint, model protocol, model default, global config, then the system default.
strategy.guideHint: Select a strategy card to apply.
strategy.cacheHitGuideTitle: Want a higher cache hit rate?
strategy.cacheHitGuideBody: Hash affinity keeps each user on a preferred Provider, making cache hits more likely by default. If you choose another strategy, enable “Provider sticky” on the route pool. Requests will prefer the last successful Provider, reducing switches and improving cache hits.
strategy.tierLevelHint: Applies only to Target ordering within this priority tier. Leave empty to inherit the route-pool default.
strategy.tierInheritReadonlyHint: Pool default and global strategy are not edited here — change them on the route pool or in Config.
strategy.tierRequiresPool: Per-tier strategy requires a route pool. Add a provider to this surface first to create one.

hash_affinity.summary: Hashes user + model + group + protocol into a fixed home: the same user always starts with the same provider; different users may land on different ones.
hash_affinity.bestFor: Keeping one user on one provider to improve upstream prompt cache hits
hash_affinity.tradeoff: With few users, traffic can look uneven

weight_priority.summary: Every request shares one fixed list: highest weight goes first, the rest are backups — who called does not matter.
weight_priority.bestFor: Clear primary/backup, predictable results, easier debugging
weight_priority.tradeoff: The primary takes almost all traffic; backups stay idle until it fails

weighted_round_robin.summary: Providers take turns as first choice by weight — with weights 3 and 1, about 3 of every 4 requests try the heavier one first.
weighted_round_robin.bestFor: Using several providers and sharing capacity or quota
weighted_round_robin.tradeoff: Each runtime instance counts on its own; cross-instance balance is approximate

weighted_random.summary: Each request draws a first provider by weight — a 60% weight tends to get about 60% of first tries over time.
weighted_random.bestFor: Proportional splits, A/B tests, or cost allocation
weighted_random.tradeoff: Two back-to-back requests may hit different providers

strategy.effectHint: Explains ordering from enabled targets only; no real request is sent.

effect.hash_affinity: The same user always starts with the same provider; if it fails, the rest of that layer are tried in order. Different users can prefer different providers.
effect.weight_priority: Numbers show the shared fixed attempt order for every request: higher weight comes first, independent of the user.
effect.weighted_round_robin: Targets in the same priority take turns as first choice by weight; the actual start depends on this runtime instance's counter.
effect.weighted_random: Each request picks its first target by weight; percentages approximate first-choice share within the priority.

strategy.priorityFirst: Strategy only orders targets inside one priority layer: Priority always wins first — the next fallback layer is used only after every target in the higher layer fails.
strategy.runtimeHealthHint: Runtime also removes circuit-open providers first, so the live order can change with provider health.
strategy.roundRobinInstanceHint: On Cloudflare Workers, each isolate keeps its own counter, so rotation is best-effort rather than globally even.
strategy.singleTargetEffect: {count} usable target(s) are available; with fewer than two, every strategy has the same first choice.
strategy.inactiveExcluded: Disabled routes or providers are excluded from this preview.
strategy.hintCache: Strategies other than Hash affinity may reduce prompt cache hit rate.
strategy.hintNoCache: Upstream has no prompt cache; prefer Weighted random or Weighted round-robin.

providerSticky.title: Provider sticky
providerSticky.tooltip: Prefer the Provider used by the last successful request. Each success restarts the sticky TTL.
providerSticky.idleTtlHint: Allowed range {min}–{max} seconds. Default {default}. Each successful request restarts the TTL. Sticky expires after the TTL passes without a request.
providerSticky.scopeHint: Prefer the Provider used by the last successful request.
providerSticky.orderPreview: When the same caller sends another request, the last successful Provider is tried first.
providerSticky.tradeoff: As long as that Provider keeps succeeding, it remains preferred. Other Providers are tried after it fails.
providerSticky.poolSharedHint: A different Provider becomes preferred after it succeeds. This setting applies to every request surface linked to this route pool.
providerSticky.requiresPool: Provider sticky requires a route pool. Add a provider to this surface first to create one.
providerSticky.distributionHint: Active bindings (valid epoch and not expired) per target. Weight share is the absolute route weight (same W as on route cards) normalized across this whole pool—not within a priority layer.
providerSticky.distributionEmpty: No targets or active bindings yet.
providerSticky.lookupHint: Enter a user email or user id to see which target they are currently stuck to.
providerSticky.lookupRequired: Enter an email or user id.
providerSticky.lookupNone: No sticky binding for this user on this pool.
providerSticky.clearConfirm: Clear this user's sticky binding? Their next request will choose a provider normally.
providerSticky.resetHint: Bumps sticky_epoch so every user reselects on the next request. Historical rows are not deleted immediately; they expire via GC or overwrite.
providerSticky.resetConfirm: Invalidate all sticky bindings for this pool? Every user will reselect a provider on their next request.
providerSticky.residualHint: Sticky is off, but {active} active and {stale} stale bindings remain. New requests are not recorded; clear leftovers if you want a clean slate.

failover.title: Failover rules
failover.readonlyHint: These rules are fixed today and not configurable yet.
failover.order: Attempt order: priority tiers high → low; within a tier, order by that tier's route strategy; skip providers in cooldown.
failover.sameLayer: Same-tier failover: 429 / 5xx / 401 / 403 / 524 / network errors try the next candidate; client errors such as 400 / 404 do not switch providers.
failover.crossLayer: Cross-tier failover: after a higher priority tier is exhausted, continue to the next priority tier (operator-defined primary/backup).
failover.attemptLimit: No fixed retry cap: every active route that is not circuit-open may be tried.
failover.circuitCooldown: Provider cooldown: 429 backs off 5s→15s→30s→60s (prefer upstream Retry-After, capped at 15 minutes); 401/403 for 5 minutes; 5xx opens for 10s after 3 consecutive failures.
failover.allBusy: If every provider is cooling down: gateway returns 429 circuit.upstream_capacity_exhausted with zero upstream calls; honor Retry-After.
failover.memoryNote: Cooldown state is in-process memory and is not shared across Cloudflare Worker isolates.
failover.imagesAbort: Image generation: client cancel or gateway timeout returns 504 and does not fail over to another provider.

playground.title: Playground
playground.subtitle: {product} — send one upstream request for a single model route. No API key billing, no api_key_request_logs, no failover.
playground.chooseRouteHint: Choose a route above to see catalog fields.
playground.sentHeadersHint: Typical driver headers plus route extras. Amber badge marks custom_params. Secrets are redacted.
playground.sentHeadersHintSent: Exact outbound headers from last Send. Amber badge marks custom_params. Secrets are redacted.
playground.sentBodyHint: Returned after Send: custom_params merged, with model and other upstream-aligned fields.
playground.sentBodyPreviewHint: Local preview: route custom_params merged (user fields win) and provider model written. After Send, this pane shows the exact upstream body.
playground.sentBodyPreviewHintForceOverride: Local preview: route custom_params merged (route fields win) and provider model written. After Send, this pane shows the exact upstream body.
playground.sentBodyEmpty: After Send, this pane shows the JSON actually sent upstream so you can verify custom_params.
playground.sentBodyInvalidJson: Fix the JSON on the left to preview the merged request body.
playground.requestTargetUrlEmpty: Select a route to preview the full upstream URL.
playground.requestTargetUrlHint: Preview from provider base_url (same join rules as Send). After Send, shows the URL actually used.
playground.requestTargetUrlRealtimeHint: WebSocket address. The underlying handshake uses HTTP GET + Upgrade; audio frames are sent after the task starts.

playground.audioTranscriptionsDashScopeHint: DashScope synchronous ASR: the Playground adapter encodes the audio as a Data URL and sends JSON upstream. No billing or request logs.

detailUx.billingOrder: Charges use Budget first, then Wallet.

fieldHints.budgetMax: The total Budget allowance available in this cycle. Leave empty for unlimited; 0 means no Budget allowance.
fieldHints.budgetSpent: The amount already used from Budget this cycle. Changing it corrects the usage total and recalculates the remaining allowance.
fieldHints.budgetBase: The allowance restored at each automatic reset. On reset, the current limit becomes this amount and Budget spent returns to 0.
fieldHints.budgetPeriod: Choose a daily, weekly, or monthly reset. No automatic reset keeps the current allowance until you change it.
fieldHints.budgetResetAt: The next automatic reset time, shown in {timezone}. It takes effect only when automatic reset is enabled.
fieldHints.walletGranted: The total amount credited to Wallet so far. Enter the new total, rather than an amount to add; saving replaces the existing total.
fieldHints.walletSpent: The total amount already used from Wallet. Changing it corrects the usage total. Balance is total granted minus total spent.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Budgets, API keys, and external identity

help.createUser: Creates a new gateway user. Email is required; all other fields are optional. To link this user to an account in another system, use the External identity section at the bottom.
help.budgetMax: Maximum available amount in the current cycle. Leave empty for unlimited.
help.budgetBase: Reference cap used when the cycle resets.
help.budgetSpent: Amount already spent from the current cycle budget.
help.budgetPeriod: Reset cycle type. none disables auto-reset.
help.budgetResetAt: Next reset time in the business timezone ({timezone}).
help.walletGranted: Cumulative Wallet credits issued. Saving replaces the absolute total; use this for operational corrections.
help.walletSpent: Cumulative amount already consumed from Wallet.
help.walletBalance: Current balance = total granted − total spent. Read-only; Wallet does not reset with the cycle or expire with the subscription.
help.metadataReplace: Saving replaces the entire metadata object. Leave empty to keep current value unchanged.
help.rateLimitRpm: Shared across all keys of this user per rolling 60-second window. Leave empty for unlimited. 0 rejects all metered calls. GET /v1/me is not counted. Per-key caps are set on each key.
help.rateLimitRpmInvalid: Rate limit must be a non-negative integer, or empty for unlimited.
help.chargedCostFactors: User-specific multipliers combine with the effective route billing multiplier using the global mode (multiply or minimum), without changing cost amounts. A route group match wins, then *, then a model-wide number. Unset uses route billing; 0 means no charge. Applies to LLM, image and audio models, not Agent Tools.

chargedCostFactors.empty: No user-specific multipliers; billing uses the effective route billing multiplier.
chargedCostFactors.noMoreGroups: Every route group for this model is already listed.

editor.defaultHint: Used for route groups without a specific override.
editor.inherited: No default multiplier. Other groups use route billing.
editor.priorityHint: A group override takes priority over the default. Without either, route billing applies.
editor.factorHint: Decimal multipliers are supported. 0 means no charge.
editor.noRouteGroups: No active route groups are available for this model.
editor.jsonHint: Read-only preview of the current form, including unsaved changes and models hidden by the filter.

insights.costNote: Catalog amount total: {standard}. Billing minus cost reflects only the recorded pricing difference, before infrastructure, taxes and unrecorded costs.
insights.qualityNote: Success rate is weighted by requests. Failover share counts requests with at least one failover (0–100%). Output speed uses only successful streams with a positive measured duration; missing measurements show —. Cache hit rate uses cache-read tokens / input tokens. Average latency includes all measured requests, including failures and cancellations.
insights.budgetNote: Budget and wallet values reflect the current account state, not a historical balance for the selected range. Users are grouped by logged email.

scope.users: Selected range, grouped by logged email. Requests without an email are excluded.
scope.reliability: Final request outcomes by provider, not individual upstream attempts. Rows are ordered by failed requests, then traffic. Low sample counts need more observation.

config.subtitle: Key-value settings shared by the {product} proxy and this admin app (no duplicate env vars)

businessTimezone.title: Business timezone
businessTimezone.description: IANA name (e.g. Asia/Shanghai). Controls the calendar day for free-tier daily quota and "today" stats on the dashboard. Invalid values fall back to UTC on the Gateway.

billingCurrency.title: Billing currency
billingCurrency.description: Only USD or CNY. Applies to pricing_profile unit prices and api_keys budget fields (per-million-token pricing). Exposed on GET /v1/me as billing_currency.

userChargedCostFactorMode.title: User-specific multiplier combination
userChargedCostFactorMode.description: Choose how user-specific multipliers combine with the effective route billing multiplier, which already includes the provider multiplier. Changes take effect in about 30 seconds.
userChargedCostFactorMode.multiplyHelp: Final billing amount = catalog amount × effective route billing multiplier × user-specific multiplier. Catalog amount uses this request’s usage and catalog prices at the time. This is the default mode.
userChargedCostFactorMode.minHelp: Final billing amount = catalog amount × min(effective route billing multiplier, user-specific multiplier). The two multipliers are not multiplied together. Catalog amount uses request usage and catalog prices at the time.

errorWebhooks.title: Proxy error webhooks
errorWebhooks.description: When the Proxy persists a row with api_key_request_logs.status = error (after billing write succeeds), it optionally POSTs to the configured robot URLs. Leave a field empty to disable that channel.
errorWebhooks.urlsNote: Webhook URLs are hidden by default. Use Show to inspect them.

routeStrategy.title: Global route strategy
routeStrategy.description: Default strategy when a model or pool has no override (system_config.ROUTE_STRATEGY).
routeStrategy.dialogHint: Choose the default strategy used when a model or pool has no override.

ux.subtitle: Manage timezone, billing, routing and error notifications. Each card saves independently.
ux.timezoneHint: Sets the calendar day used by daily quotas and usage reports.
ux.currencyHint: The currency used for model prices, budgets and charges.
ux.billingModeHint: Choose how route and user multipliers combine. Updates take effect in about 30 seconds.
ux.routeHint: The default strategy for models and pools without an override.
ux.webhookHint: Send failed-request alerts to WeCom or Feishu. Leave a URL empty to disable that channel.
ux.multiplySummary: Multiply the route factor by the user factor.
ux.minSummary: Use the smaller of the route and user factors.

config.title: Tools
config.subtitle: Configure product tools under /v1/tools/* (engine, API key, unit prices). Settings are stored in system_config and share the user chat budget (charged only).

providerCards.priceLegend: S Standard · C Charged · M Metered
providerCards.selectHint: Click a provider to open the configuration drawer. Changes apply only after you save.

webSearch.title: Web search
webSearch.description: Powers POST /v1/tools/web-search. Choose an implemented engine only—free text is rejected. Leave the API key empty and save to clear it (endpoint returns 503 until set again).
webSearch.descriptionCatalog: Powers POST /v1/tools/web-search. Configure each engine’s API key and three unit prices, then save & activate one card. Only charged hits user budget. Engines without a key cannot be activated.
webSearch.needKeyToActivate: Add an API key to at least one engine before saving.
webSearch.apiKeyHint: Required for the tool to accept traffic. Cleared keys fall back to nothing (no env).

providerGuide.title: Search engine guide
providerGuide.subtitle: Index / sources and when to pick each engine. Not a direct Baidu or Google API.
providerGuide.disclaimer: None of these call Baidu or Google official search APIs. Each uses its own or partner web index; result URLs may still point at baidu.com, google.com, etc.

bocha.summary: AI-oriented Chinese search engine with its own large web index (positioned as a domestic Bing Search API alternative).
bocha.sources: Hundreds of millions to ~10B web pages plus partner content (news, encyclopedia, short video, weather, academic, etc.). Not Baidu/Google.
bocha.bestFor: China-region users, Chinese queries, domestic compliance.

tavily.summary: LLM-oriented retrieval layer: search + extract + rank in one call. Built for agents/RAG, not a classic SERP dump.
tavily.sources: Own crawler plus third-party aggregation (often associated with independent indexes such as Brave). Not an official Google/Baidu API.
tavily.bestFor: International region, English research, agent workflows.

cleversee.summary: Alibaba CleverSee (开析) AI-native web search with mainland_china / global region modes.
cleversee.sources: Alibaba’s own AI search index. Docs do not claim Baidu or Google backends. Gateway default is mainland_china; domain allow-lists switch to global.
cleversee.bestFor: When you need an explicit China vs global region switch on Alibaba Cloud.

tencent_wsa.summary: Tencent Cloud Web Search API (WSA), officially based on Sogou Search.
tencent_wsa.sources: Open web via Sogou plus Tencent ecosystem (Tencent News, Sogou Baike, Penguin accounts). Higher tiers add VR/authority verticals.
tencent_wsa.bestFor: China Chinese web as an alternative to Bocha; strong Sogou/Tencent content mix.

webFetch.title: Web fetch
webFetch.description: Powers POST /v1/tools/web-fetch. Choose an implemented scraper only—free text is rejected. Leave the API key empty and save to clear it (endpoint returns 503 until set again).
webFetch.descriptionCatalog: Powers POST /v1/tools/web-fetch. Configure each scraper’s API key and three unit prices, then save & activate one card. Only charged hits user budget. Scrapers without a key cannot be activated.
webFetch.needKeyToActivate: Add an API key to at least one provider before saving.
webFetch.apiKeyHint: Required for the tool to accept traffic. Cleared keys fall back to nothing (no env).

webDeepSearch.title: Web deep search
webDeepSearch.descriptionCatalog: Powers POST /v1/tools/web-deep-search. Search-and-read engines (Firecrawl Search / Jina Search) return page content with results—heavier and costlier than plain web search. Configure each provider, then save & activate one card.
webDeepSearch.needKeyToActivate: Add an API key to at least one provider before saving.

aiDetection.title: AI detection
aiDetection.descriptionCatalog: Powers POST /v1/tools/ai-detection. Multi-provider catalog: configure credentials and three unit prices per engine, then save & activate one card. Billing is by character units (billingUnitChars); totals scale metered/standard/charged. Currently only Tencent Cloud TMS is implemented.
aiDetection.needKeyToActivate: Add credentials to at least one implemented engine before saving.

invocations.title: Tool invocations
invocations.subtitle: Calls billed as provider octafuse-tools (model_id tool:*). Click a row to inspect query and result summary. Same underlying rows as Request Logs.
invocations.empty: No tool invocations in this range.

routeFactors.title: Route multipliers
routeFactors.body:
Route cards show effective billing and cost multipliers relative to each period’s catalog prices.
Effective billing multiplier = active provider multiplier × billing multiplier; cost is calculated the same way. Outside provider validity, ×1 applies. Hover over a multiplier for its calculation and validity dates.
Periods are previewed as of now; only the Current row applies now. User-specific multipliers are excluded from the preview and are combined at billing time according to the global mode.

unitPrices.title: Route unit prices
unitPrices.body:
Billing unit price = period catalog unit price × effective billing multiplier.
Cost unit price = period catalog unit price × effective cost multiplier.
These are prices per unit of usage, not request amounts; user-specific multipliers are excluded.

catalog.title: Catalog prices
catalog.body:
Catalog prices are the model’s base unit prices. Period catalog unit price = base catalog unit price × catalog time multiplier.
Provider, billing, cost and user-specific multipliers are excluded.

amounts.title: Billing and cost amounts
amounts.body:
Catalog amount uses request usage and catalog unit prices at request time, including catalog time multipliers.
Billing amount applies the active route rules and user-specific multipliers. Cost amount applies active route cost rules and is unaffected by user-specific multipliers.
A ratio next to a logged amount is amount ÷ catalog amount: a result ratio, not a configured multiplier. It is omitted when catalog amount is zero.

profit.title: Gross profit
profit.body:
Gross profit = billing amount − cost amount.
This is the recorded pricing difference, before infrastructure, taxes and other unrecorded expenses.

playground.title: Playground billing
playground.body: Playground calls the selected provider directly without gateway billing. Usage and route pricing configuration are shown for inspection, not as user charges. The upstream provider may still charge for the call.

simulator.title: Simulator billing
simulator.body:
Simulator sends real gateway requests with the selected API key; billing and logging apply.
Response usage is usage information only. Verify billing and cost amounts in request logs, or Tools invocation records for Agent Tools.
